subject: Unexpected charges after legacy->new endpoint migration
messages:
From: Thomas Greene <t.greene@spectralabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts@spectralabs.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected charges after migration to new endpoint

Hi Soojin,

We noticed a sizeable overage on the Sept invoice after we migrated some traffic from your legacy API (v1) to the new /v2/generate endpoint last week. Our engineering team only started hitting /v2 around 2026-09-18 14:00 UTC, but the invoice appears to include tokens from both endpoints overlapping during a short window.

Attached is a screenshot of the billing summary and a sample of our internal request ids (request-id: sp-9a4f, sp-9a7c). The spike corresponds to 2026-09-18 14:00-14:12 UTC. From our side there were ~18k tokens during that window; the bill shows ~42k tokens attributed.

Can you help investigate whether our usage was double-counted during migration or if there's an attribution rule we missed? Also, what is the VAT treatment for the credit if one is issued? We are an EU-registered company (VAT ID: IT123456789).

Thanks,
Thomas Greene
Head of Engineering
Spectra Labs
[Attachment: billing_screenshot.png]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Greene <t.greene@spectralabs.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, accounts@spectralabs.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges after migration to new endpoint

Hi Thomas — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I’m sorry for the surprise billing. I’m looping in our billing lead, Rishi, so we can pull the raw metering logs and validate attribution during that window.

Quick asks to speed this up:
- Can you confirm the Spectra account ID you used with us (the one shown in the Console under "Account")?
- If you can, paste 2–3 example request-ids (you gave two already — if there are any more from ~14:00 UTC that helps).

We will:
- Pull a detailed per-request export for 2026-09-17 through 2026-09-19, including endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, and meter_bucket.
- Check for any known batch-boundary duplication or attribution overlap between v1 and v2 at the time you migrated.

Rishi — can you confirm we have a script-ready export? Monica from CS, I’ve added you in case we need a reconciliation call with their finance team.

I’ll follow up with initial findings by end of day.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Greene <t.greene@spectralabs.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, accounts@spectralabs.com
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected charges after migration to new endpoint

Hi all — I pulled the per-request metering export and did a focused audit for 2026-09-18 13:50–14:20 UTC. Findings (summary):

1) Root cause: At 14:00 UTC Spectra sent a small percentage of traffic to both the legacy v1 endpoint and the new /v2/generate during a ~9 minute rollout window. Our metering backend historically counted tokens per request and then assigned them to a "meter_bucket" derived from the active endpoint id at ingestion. There was a race where both the legacy and v2 emitters reported the same session_id for a handful of requests. In those cases the metering service created two records for the same logical session: one attributed to the legacy bucket and one to the v2 bucket.

2) Impact: The duplicate records amount to ~23,400 tokens during the affected window. That matches the delta you reported (approx 42k billed vs ~18k actual on your side).

3) Corrective action: We de-duplicated the affected records and regenerated a provisional usage export (attached). We plan to issue a one-time pro forma credit for the double-counted tokens: USD 1,220.00. I’ve prepared a draft credit note and placed a HubSpot credit record here: https://app.hubspot.com/records/SPEC-4829/credits/CR-1023

4) VAT treatment: Because Spectra Labs is an EU-registered company (you provided a VAT ID), the credit will be issued without VAT (reverse-charge applies). We will need a copy of your VAT registration (VAT ID: IT123456789) on file before we finalize the credit note.

Attachments: redwood_usage_export_20260920.csv (per-request rows flagged), draft_credit_note_20260924.pdf

Next steps:
- Thomas: confirm VAT ID and whether we should route the credit to the Sept invoice or as a standalone credit note for application in October.
- Monica: please review the draft credit note and confirm wording/amount for accounting.

I’ll hold issuance until we have confirmation on VAT and routing.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Billing & Revenue Operations
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_usage_export_20260920.csv]
